paper_metadata.title: A 1-MHz-Bandwidth Second-Order Continuous-Time Quadrature Bandpass Sigma–Delta Modulator for Low-IF Radio Receivers
paper_metadata.abstract: This paper presents a quadrature bandpass modulator with continuous-time architecture. Due to the continuous-time architecture and the inherent anti-aliasing filter, the proposed modulator needs no additional anti-aliasing filter in front of the modulator in contrast to quadrature bandpass modulators with switched-capacitor architectures. The second-order modulator digitizes complex analog input signals at 1-MHz intermediate frequency and operates within a clock frequency range of 25–100 MHz. The modulator chip Fig. 1. Low-IF receiver architecture. achieves a peak signal-to-noise-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 56.7 dB and a dynamic range of 63.8 dB within a 1 –MHz signal bandwidth and at a clock frequency of 100 MHz. Furthermore, it provides and a low-IF of 1 MHz results in an ADC bandwidth of about an image rejection of at least 40 dB. The 0.65m BiCMOS chip 1.5 MHz. consumes 21.8 mW at 2.7-V supply voltage.
